idiom_name: static Func<T, T> Id = static x => x — cached generic delegate (no BCL identity exists)
implementation_notes: C# has no identity function anywhere in the base class library — the .NET libraries ship no standalone equivalent of Java's Function.identity(), and the language team declined to add one (dotnet/csharplang discussion #4412); the idiomatic replacement is a one-expression lambda: an inline x => x key selector for LINQ operators (OrderBy, GroupBy, Select) or one shared public static readonly Func<T, T> Id field in a generic static class for strategy/pipeline APIs, marked with the C# 9 static lambda modifier so it cannot capture and is cached by the Roslyn compiler instead of allocating per call. A companion C#-specific form is the expression-tree identity Expression<Func<T, T>> e = x => x (body equal to its ParameterExpression), required when the pipeline is IQueryable-based because a delegate cannot be translated; the classic named-identity-facility structure stays justified only as the single canonical symbol of a shared utilities library, since the language offers none and ad-hoc local definitions fragment.
pitfalls: Value-type copies: invoking Func<T, T> with a struct argument loads it by value, so the "zero-cost" identity copies the entire struct on every call (a large struct makes Id measurably expensive), and a non-generic object Identity(object x) boxes value types on every invocation.

Hidden capture kills compiler caching: a lambda that accidentally closes over a local or this allocates a fresh display class plus delegate instance per execution in hot pipelines; the C# 9 static modifier (static x => x) makes non-capture a compile-time guarantee.

Illegal as a default parameter value: void M(Func<T, T> f = x => x) does not compile because default values must be compile-time constants — the csharplang #4412 discussion; use an overload, or null combined with f ?? Fn<T>.Id at the call boundary.

Expression-tree identity is not executable: Expression<Func<T, T>> builds a data structure that must be .Compile()d before invocation and is not convertible to/from Func<T, T>; passing an identity tree to an IQueryable provider means it gets translated, never invoked.

No canonical name, so every codebase invents one (Id, Identity, Passthrough, NO_OP) and the common identifier id collides with entity-key properties (EDID/UUID columns), making search for existing identity helpers unreliable.
